note: Append one entry per completed HLT load run. Temporary tracking file for the 1000 TPS push.

runs.headline: Same-J swap baseline after the reliable-layer removal
runs.detail: Deleting the reliable delivery layer, moving keccak to WASM, hand-writing the ABI and using native ECDSA took matched swaps from 3 to 249 per second. The profile went flat afterwards: no single site dominates any more.

runs.headline: Profile advertises only pinned hubs, capped at 100
runs.detail: A Hub's gossip Profile carried one row per Account and crossed the 10 KB storage leaf at ~34 accounts, halting every observing Runtime. Only pinned counterparties are advertised now, so a 100-user population no longer trips it. The run still died: a second agent was rewriting the mempool mid-run.

runs.headline: Frame delay floor of 100 ms on the Hub
runs.detail: A frame costs about the same whether it carries one transaction or a hundred, so holding frames back should be free throughput. Routes converged in 901 ms and payments flowed, then the Hub halted: batching pushed 49 prepared HTLCs into one 36 KB replay leaf against a 10 KB cap.

runs.headline: Batching walls cleared: HTLC leaves, paged manifests, duplicate collapse
runs.detail: Four faults surfaced the moment frames carried real batches: prepared HTLCs shared one 36 KB record, the manifest naming them reached 20.9 KB, and a retransmitted proposal halted the Runtime outright. First green payment run afterwards, still limited by the driver rather than the Hub.

runs.headline: Payments clear 30/s with every payment delivered
runs.detail: 32 senders offering one payment per second delivered 160 of 160 in 4.9 s. The Hub spent 34 frames on them, 4.7 payments per frame, so the ceiling is still the driver's offered rate and not the Hub.

runs.headline: Same-J swaps clear 30/s on the same commit
runs.detail: 64 users settled 160 of 160 swaps: 36.0 matched per second and 32.2 fully settled. Both workloads now hold above the 30/s mark on one Hub, and neither is Hub-limited yet.

runs.headline: 128 users saturate the stand, not the Hub
runs.detail: 64 senders offered 64 payments per second and 320 of 320 were delivered, but only at 29.1 per second while 28 of the machine's 32 cores were busy. Doubling the population did not raise throughput: one OS process per user costs about a fifth of a core just to exist.

runs.headline: Payments clear 50/s at 100 users; per-payment cost model measured
runs.detail: 50 senders delivered 2000 of 2000 at 49.5/s (offered 50). Memoized ECDSA signatures, HTLC layer decryption and the account state root, but each 3-7% win was invisible in run totals: the Hub costs 100 ms fixed + 5.6 ms per account output per frame (~26 ms CPU/payment), the lanes 42 ms fixed + 10 ms per entity frame (~80 ms). Gossip fan-out turned out to be O(N^2): the relay pushed every profile change to every client.

runs.headline: Pull-only gossip: relay pushes nothing, users ask for chains and masked pages
runs.detail: Same 100-user run, same 49.5/s, but lane CPU fell 220 s -> 185 s (-16%) and the Hub 102 s -> 96 s: profile verification left the daemons. Profiles are now served only on request (hubs set, ids with depth 1..3, routeTo route chains, masked prefix pages), non-hub profiles announce hourly or on topology change, capacities floor to 000. Three pull-only regressions surfaced and were fixed on the way: a profile-clock watermark hid slow-clock profiles forever (relay receipt cursor now), the cursor was keyed by an id hello_ack never carried, and the lookup budget counted every poll.

runs.headline: 200 users in one process: works, but one sender daemon carries ~40 senders at 1 tx/s
runs.detail: 200 users hosted 200 per daemon, 100 offered per second, 4000 of 4000 delivered but only at 53/s: the sender daemon spends ~24 ms CPU per payment (entity frame + HTLC + storage), so 100 senders at 1 tx/s need 2.4 cores in a single-threaded process. Hub cost per payment dropped to 14 ms because 40+ payments now share one frame. Fine for real users at 0.1 tx/s; for the 100 tps bench the population must spread over more processes.

runs.headline: Payments reach 100/s: 92.6 delivered of 100 offered, Hub now the wall
runs.detail: 200 users over 5 daemons (40 per process), 100 senders at 1 tx/s: 4000 of 4000 delivered in 43.2 s. The Hub ran at 100% for the whole window (453 ms wall per frame x 94 frames) at 12.8 ms CPU per payment; its profile is flat: radix rootHash 11%, hanko verify+recover 16%, account state root 8%, entity state hash 7%, storage encode 7%, followups 6%. 500/s needs ~2.5 ms per payment on the Hub, i.e. structural cuts, not one patch.

runs.headline: Same-J swaps hold 100/s matched on the same commit
runs.detail: 200 users, 40 per process, 100 swaps submitted per second for 40 rounds: matched kept pace with submission the whole run (in-flight steady at 80-180, 3860 of 4000 matched at the last window, all settled at quiescence). Hub CPU 125 s for the run against 98 s for payments; both workloads now hold at the 100/s mark on one Hub.

runs.headline: 500 users green, 54.5/s: driver waited for commandObserved each round
runs.detail: 5000/5000 delivered, offered 500/s, Hub height 393→611 (~23 payments/frame). No halt after Entity wire-fit. Round lag grew to 66 s because each of 20 rounds waited for all 250 commands to commit before the next. WAL 28→248 MB.

runs.headline: Batched hub-poll payments: 149/s at 200 users
runs.detail: Grow-fit plus fire-and-forget enqueue (pending) plus hub lockBook/credit poll. 1000/1000 in 6.7 s, Hub height 299→313 (14 frames, ~71 payments/frame). Offered-rate field still 100/s because cadence is 1 Hz; the driver submitted all ten rounds in one command per sender. WAL 13→30 MB.

runs.headline: First complete 500-user payments run: 130.5/s, 15000/15000 delivered
runs.detail: Unified proposal path (single-signer = build proposal → commit immediately, no precommit round). Fixes: mempool prune by frame.txs; htlc_resolve direct hashlock lookup (was ~50% hub CPU); htlc_lock capacity as retry (MAX_ACCOUNT_HTLC_LOCKS=32 stalled at 32 payments/sender); cascade guard scales with replicas; wireFit ratio fit with hasReplayEntityContext; content-keyed onion decrypt memo; secret-ack timeout 120 s; dispute-start batch re-arm. 114.9 s, exit 0, no hub warnings. Hub: 30 heavy frames = 78 s; wireFit 44 s (infraMaterialize 526 calls, avg 36 ms, max 3.3 s), frameApply 20 s.

runs.headline: Native X25519 for onion layers: 186.7/s at 500 users
runs.detail: node:crypto diffieHellman replaces the pure-JS noble ladder for HTLC onion and p2p session ECDH (25 us vs 330 us per scalar mult; identical RFC 7748 bytes, browsers fall back to noble). Also dropped the duplicate multi-MB canonical encode after infra-context validation and added sub-phase perf counters (infraMaterialize.htlc/validate/authority, wireFit.measure, proposal.assertHtlc). 7500/7500 in 40.2 s (30 rounds), exit 0. Hub phase totals: wireFit 4.0 s (was 7.5 s), infraMaterialize.htlc 2.6 s (was 5.7 s), assertHtlc 1.5 s.

runs.headline: Hub is now the wall: 248.8/s at 500 users with 10 lanes (50 users each)
runs.detail: Same code as aaf5db645 plus perf-snapshot throttling (percentile sort on every frame was ~9% of Hub CPU under XLN_RUNTIME_APPLY_PROFILE) and no op-counters. Lanes at 100 users each were co-limiting (5 lanes peaked at 125-146% CPU); with 10 lanes the lanes idle at 20-40% avg while Hub main thread sits at 100-125% for the whole 30 s window. 7500/7500 in 30.1 s, exit 0. Hub CPU profile (m500m): storage 22% (account envelope trie 11%), state roots 14%, hanko verify 4.4%, HTLC materialize+replay 6.9%, own-frame validation/measure 4%.
